verdict.rationale: Grok Bot lets users create named Bots by describing the job, and each Bot keeps its own memory, files and preferences. Bots can be duplicated or shared as templates, and Team Bots can be invited into shared channels. Community users confirm that each bot owns its own context and domain. However, there are no in-depth docs on authoring explicit custom instructions, attaching a curated knowledge base, or what a shared template contains. missing for 10: documented custom-instruction/system-prompt configuration, explicit knowledge-base upload or attachment per Bot, detail on template-sharing scope and permissions, independent hands-on corroboration of sharing.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can build and share custom assistants with their own instructions and knowledge

citations.quote: Create a Bot, describe the job, and grant access as it asks.
A named Bot keeps its memory, files, browser sessions, and preferences across sessions instead of resetting on every task.
Share a template when someone else should start from the same Bot.
Duplicate a Bot when you want the same role as a starting point for a different scope
